title: Barefoot Investor Scott Pape calls out Australia's superannuation funds
text:
By Ashley Nickel for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 02:45 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 02:45 GMT, February 9, 2025
Barefoot’s investor, Scott Pape, has signed up for Australian retirement fund managers in his last column, after a reader’s concerns about the performance of his retirement.
‘I am writing you because I am worried about my super. I am with Australiansuper, and lately, they have had some fillings. ‘ The reader explained.
‘They lost $ 1 billion in a private capital agreement, and this week it was reported that they invested $ 500 million in Nvidia just before it crashed! His returns have not been great, so I wonder what you would suggest. ‘
Pape advised to judge Australiansuper based only on some bad investments.
“Its portfolio is so large that a pair of financial fireballs will not be as much as an ash for their general returns,” he wrote.
But Mr. Pape also questioned why retirement funds chose to choose actions instead of indices, which are low cost and have been shown to carry out professional fund managers.
‘This is what always baffled me from the super industry: why are they trying to choose the winners?
‘Evidence is clear as crystal: index investment works. In the long run, the low cost index funds exceed professional fund managers eight times from every 10.
‘And, the more money you have to invest, the more difficult it will be to overcome the market. Ask Warren Buffett: he has not exceeded the index in 20 years. Your advice? Stay with indices funds.
Financial Advisor Scott Pape (in the photo) advised the followers to consider the low -cost index options of their super background on the professional fund managers
Pape added that retirement companies are paying huge salaries to fund managers, who historically have had a lower long -term performance.
‘So this is the choice that super funds are making: invest in ultra -low cost index funds or trust our’ experts’ team (which collectively cost hundreds of millions in salaries every year) choose investments for you.
‘But here is the capture: these experts only have a probability of two in 10 to overcome the long -term index. And to cover their salaries, they will have to charge you nine times more in rates than index funds.
‘Who in his healthy judgment would take that deal? Answer: almost all super important funds in the country.
Instead of leaving the retirement company together, Pape suggested that the reader consider the Australiansuper index fund options.
“I don’t care Australiansuper, especially its low -cost index offers,” he said.
The main super funds from Australia during the last decade 1. Balanced hostplus : 8.4 percent of average annual returns
2. Australian retirement trust – Super balanced savings : 8.3 percent
3. Australiansuper – balanced : 8.1 percent
4. Unisuper – balanced : 7.9 percent
5. CBU – Growth (my super) : 7.8 percent
6. Super vision – balanced growth : 7.8 percent
7. Hostplus – balanced indexed : 7.7 percent
8. HESTA – Balanced growth : 7.7 percent
9. Conscious Super – Future Saver : 7.7 percent
10. Careuper – balanced : 7.6 percent
